scope: Per-page layout parity with the ONLYOFFICE table-flow kernel: per-cell page state, row fragments, natural 546-page pagination; measured against desktop Word for the real 1.2MB proposal

method.word: Word COM: for each page, range from GoTo(page) start to GoTo(page+1) start, text normalized (whitespace collapsed, max 1200 chars); 546 pages
method.web: headless Edge CDP: per .op-word-page innerText excluding header/footer/notes/page-number/ink/watermark/floats (Word main-story Range excludes text boxes)
method.metric: Dice coefficient over lowercased word sets; same index plus best of offsets -2..+2

greedyWithoutTarget.note: natural height fill aligns more pages with Word but overshoots by 4 pages; the 546 target rebalances breaks and lowers page content overlap to 11/546

rowFlow.api: flowRow(cells, states, available) with CellPageState { cursor, pagesCount, firstPageHasContent }, CellPageSlice { start, end, clipTop, clipBottom } and paginateTableRows() reporting TableRowsBottom
rowFlow.tests: offline kernel tests: tall row 10 lines x 20px on 100px page -> 5/5 lines, PagesCount 2; mixed cells 6/2/0 lines -> 3/1/0 per page; captured cell lines from 13 real tables -> deterministic, 0 lines lost, max fragment <= contentHeight
rowFlow.default: rowFlow enabled by default; paragraph metricScale 0.95 and table line scale 1.348 with keepNext lookahead give 546 pages without docProps target balancing

cause.tableRows: docx has 951 w:trHeight rows (largest 8419 twips = 561px); the renderer ignored them, so Word table rows were taller than the web rows and page starts drifted
cause.imagesTextboxes: Word main-story Range excludes text inside drawing text boxes while the web page includes them; image/paragraph vertical space also differs
cause.sections: Word sections start at pages 1/534/542/544/546; only section 4 is landscape (792x612pt, pages 544-545). The renderer uses the final portrait sectPr for every page, so those 2 landscape pages render portrait
cause.tableWidths: document has 5886 w:tcW, 1 w:gridSpan and 4 w:vMerge; the checked tables use tcW matching their tblGrid percentages, so ignoring tcW does not explain the drift
cause.tableFont: DOM check of the services table shows 18.67px = 14pt, matching Word COM; the table has no w:tblStyle so cells already inherit Normal 14pt
cause.conclusion: The per-cell flow + per-section geometry + paragraph metricScale 0.95 + keepNext now reaches 546 naturally and raises page content overlap to 52/546 pages >= 0.8 (mean 0.528). The dominant residual is Word line/text metrics and image/paragraph spacing around the architecture figures

implementation.rowHeights: parse w:trPr/w:trHeight w:val (twips -> px /15) per row into WordBlock.rowHeights and WordNestedTable.rowHeights
implementation.render: tableTemplate applies [style.height.px] to <tr> and passes the sliced rowHeights for page table fragments and nested tables
implementation.effect: same-index pages with Dice >= 0.8 rose 8 -> 11; page count remains 546 deterministic
implementation.tableStyleResolution: resolveTableStyle now bases styled tables on the document default paragraph style instead of raw docDefaults, so cell paragraphs without direct size do not fall back to 12pt; this sample's tables have no tblStyle and already render 14pt, so the page metrics are unchanged
implementation.sectionGeometry: blocks carry sectionIndex from paragraph-level sectPr; pagination switches contentHeight per section before creating the page; article width/min-height/padding come from the page section. Verified pages 544-545 render 1056x816 landscape and page 546 renders 816x1056 portrait, matching Word sections 4/5 at pages 544/546
implementation.keepNext: parse w:keepNext from pPr and styles; pagination looks ahead to the next block height and moves the keepNext paragraph to a new page when the pair would overflow. This pulls the architecture headings/images together like Word and raises page overlap 44 -> 52/546
implementation.contextualSpacingExperiment: ListParagraph carries w:contextualSpacing (Word suppresses space between same-style list items). Applying it removed the 10.7px after-space but dropped parity to 47-48/546 >= 0.8 (mean 0.505-0.507) after recalibration; the experiment was reverted
implementation.lineHeightExperiment: Measurement showed web one-line paragraphs are 25.2px while computed line-height is 21.24px; the cause is CSS min-height 1.35em. Removing it and adding inline min-height=line-height plus contextual spacing (1/3 residual) dropped page count to 543 and parity to 41/546 (mean 0.505) even after table scale 1.353 restored 546 pages; reverted. The 25.2px line box currently compensates for missing image/paragraph spacing elsewhere, so changing it alone lowers parity
implementation.headerRepeatExperiment: Root cause for the architecture page shift: Word repeats w:tblHeader rows on each page of a split table (services table on page 7 starts 286px down because the header repeats), while the web renderer does not. Implemented tblHeader parsing and repeated header rows in paginated fragments; the synthetic fragments destabilized settlement (127 -> 46 pages, settled false) because repeated headers were measured as new rows. Repeat was disabled and the build returned to 546/52 pages; the parser now records headerRows for a future stable implementation

checks.qaPaginationTwice: 546 pages both loads, equalPageCount true, equalTableCount true, deterministic true, exceptions 0 (rowFlow default, no docProps target)

wordPageMap.conclusion: 460 of 529 mapped breaks start inside a table row, not at a row boundary; the renderer only splits tables between rows, so a faithful Word map requires per-row vertical slicing across all cells (row splits) plus mid-paragraph slicing

openSourceReference.project: ONLYOFFICE sdkjs (AGPL), sparse checkout of word/Editor
files: word/Editor/Table/TableRecalculate.js: bNextPage / LastRowSplit / continue same row (line ~3034-3094)
word/Editor/Paragraph.js: line spacing and line layout
openSourceReference.algorithm: Each cell content is recalculated against the page Y limit; the row bottom is the max cell bottom on that page; when content exceeds the page, LastRowSplit is set and the same row continues on the next page; cells independently expose their per-page content bounds
openSourceReference.attempt: Two ports tried: (1) split from measured paragraph heights, (2) measured per-cell line offsets, rebuilt one-row fragments, and moved the settle signature to stored measurements so split fragments would not destabilize it. Isolated checks preserved all 300/600 test characters
openSourceReference.result: The pure kernel is stable: offline tests preserve all lines and are deterministic on 13 captured real tables. Integrated per-cell flow with paragraph metricScale 0.95, table line scale 1.348 and keepNext lookahead gives 546 pages without docProps target balancing; per-section page geometry renders pages 544-545 landscape and 546 portrait like Word. Dice >= 0.8 rises 11 -> 52/546 and mean Dice 0.435 -> 0.528. Per-page parity is improved but not yet 100%
openSourceReference.next: Port private_RecalculatePage together with its per-cell content/clip state instead of splitting rows from measured heights only

audit.wordGroups: TR-S12-002 now records Word 20 full / 1 partial (W-A21 pagination: total page count matches, per-page layout does not) / 0 not done
audit.otherApps: the remaining 20 partial + 22 not-done groups in TR-S12-002 belong to Excel, PowerPoint, PDF and shell; they are outside the Word slice but mean overall Office-webapp parity is not 100%
acceptedGaps: spellcheck/grammar rule-based instead of Microsoft Editor (accepted)
VBA macros cannot run in the browser (accepted, same as Word for the web)

remaining: Per-page content parity is 52/546 pages >= 0.8 with mean Dice 0.528; the remaining differences are Word line/text metrics and image/paragraph spacing
